chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Sinan who said:

I heard Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) saying: 'The constitution of the body is based on four elements: among them is the air, without which the soul cannot survive except by its flow, and it expels from the body what is in it of disease and decay; and the earth, which generates dryness and heat; and the food, from which blood is generated. Do you not see that it goes to the stomach, which nourishes it until it becomes soft, then it clarifies, so the natural process takes its clarified state as blood; then the residue descends with the water, and it generates phlegm.'

key_terms.طَبَائِعُ الْجِسْمِ: constitution or nature of the body

ai.seo_question: What are the four elements that constitute the human body according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam Al-Reza (AS) outlines the humoral theory of the human body, identifying air, earth, food, and water as the four constitutive elements that govern physiological health. He details the digestive process where food transforms into blood in the stomach, while the lower portion yields phlegm, reflecting the Greco-Arabic medical understanding prevalent in Shia scholarly tradition. This narration underscores the holistic view of the body as a microcosm of natural elements, linking physical well-being to spiritual and cosmic order.
